security_spec.violation_condition: On RV32 with 34-bit physical addresses, if the kernel configures a TOR PMP entry intending to cover the top of physical memory (addresses 0x3_FFFF_FFFC–0x3_FFFF_FFFF), the pmpaddr register cannot represent 2^34 as the top bound, so the uppermost word is left unmatched by any TOR entry. If this region contains sensitive data (e.g., a page table, trampoline, or device MMIO) and no other PMP entry covers it, S/U-mode accesses to that word will either fail open (if no PMP entry matches, which denies S/U access by default) or fall through to a lower-priority rule, depending on PMP configuration.
security_spec.summary: RV32 TOR PMP entries cannot cover the uppermost word of 34-bit physical address space; the kernel must use NAPOT or accept the gap when configuring PMP for the highest physical page

findings.finding: M-mode PMP initialization correctly uses NAPOT encoding (PMP_A_NAPOT) with pmpaddr0=-1 to cover the entire physical address space, avoiding the RV32 TOR limitation where the uppermost word (0x3_FFFF_FFFC-0x3_FFFF_FFFF) cannot be matched by any TOR entry because pmpaddr registers cannot represent 2^34 as a top bound. The spec note at machine.adoc:3508-3518 explicitly documents this TOR limitation and recommends NAPOT as the workaround — which this code follows.
findings.snippet:
li a0, -1
csrw CSR_PMPADDR0, a0
li a0, (PMP_A_NAPOT | PMP_R | PMP_W | PMP_X)
csrw CSR_PMPCFG0, a0

spec_citations.excerpt: [norm:pmp_addr_encoding] Each PMP address register encodes bits 33-2 of a 34-bit physical address for RV32

[norm:pmp_a_field_tor] If TOR is selected, the associated address register forms the top of the address range, and the preceding PMP address register forms the bottom of the address range. If PMP entry i's A field is set to TOR, the entry matches any address y such that pmpaddr[i-1] ≤ y < pmpaddr[i]

It is not possible to represent the address 2^34 as the top of a range, so, for example, in an RV32 system with 34-bit physical addresses, a TOR PMP cannot be used to give less-privileged modes access to the uppermost word of memory. Either a NAPOT PMP can be used, or that memory can be left inaccessible to less-privileged modes.

findings.finding: PMP_A_TOR (0x08) is defined alongside PMP_A_NA4 (0x10) and PMP_A_NAPOT (0x18) as part of the standard RISC-V PMP address-matching mode constants. TOR is not used anywhere in the kernel code — only NAPOT is used in head.S. The constant's presence does not constitute a bug; it is a faithful definition of the ISA's encoding. Future code that might use TOR on RV32 would need to account for the 2^34 top-bound limitation.

spec_citations.excerpt: A field encoding: TOR (A=1) — Top of range
